instructions: About 30 minutes before you start, take the 1/2 cup butter and the 2 eggs out of the fridge so they come to room temperature.
Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle, and line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
In a medium bowl, whisk together 2 cups of the flour, the 2 tsp baking powder and the 1/2 tsp salt.
In a large bowl, beat the butter with 1 cup of the sugar using a hand mixer on medium speed for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time. Then beat in the 1/2 cup milk, 1 tsp vanilla and 1/8 tsp almond extract. It may look a little curdled, and that's fine.
Tip the flour mixture into the bowl and fold it in with a spatula until you can't see any dry flour. Stop there. More mixing makes the muffins tough.
In a small bowl, toss 2 1/4 cups of the blueberries with the last 1 tbsp flour until they're lightly coated. Fold them gently into the batter.
Divide the batter between the 12 cups. Sprinkle the last 1 tbsp sugar over the tops.
Put the pan in the oven and turn the heat down to 375°F straight away. Bake for 18 to 23 minutes, until the tops are golden and a toothpick in the middle of one comes out clean.
Leave them in the pan for 2 minutes, then move them to a wire rack to cool.

Serve them warm or at room temperature, with the rest of the blueberries. Keep cooled muffins in a sealed container for up to 2 days, or freeze them in a bag for up to 1 month and thaw them on the counter.
method_notes: All three cream soft butter with sugar, beat in eggs, add a liquid dairy and fold in the flour just until it disappears before the berries go in. Spend With Pennies (the lead) uses milk with a little almond extract, tosses the berries in a spoonful of flour, sugars the tops and starts the oven at 400°F before dropping it to 375°F for a taller dome. Baker by Nature makes a richer batter with brown sugar, sour cream and a pinch of nutmeg and allspice, and King Arthur uses sour cream or yogurt with a thick, almost cookie-dough batter at 375°F. This one follows the lead, and the batch of 12 covers several breakfasts for four.
